amqp091-go: Pre-negotiation frame limit is not enforced to 4KB

Aliases: CVE-2026-107386

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • github.com/rabbitmq/amqp091-go — fixed in 1.14.0

## Summary The frame-size mitigation released in `amqp091-go` v1.13.0 can be bypassed before `connection.tune` completes. A malicious or compromised AMQP peer can send only a seven-byte body-frame header containing a large attacker-controlled `uint32` payload length. The client allocates a slice of that declared length before it verifies that the payload exists or rejects the frame for its invalid protocol state. The bypass occurs because `Connection.maxFrameSize` starts at zero. The reader interprets zero as both “negotiated unlimited” and “not negotiated yet,” and skips the pre-allocation size check in either case. `Open` starts the reader goroutine before negotiation and does not store a limit until after it receives `connection.tune`. This remains reachable even if the caller explici…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-pc5q-qfxp-ggqv: Coraza: jsDecode Off-by-One in Octal Escape Handling Enables WAF Bypass
entry.content:
Coraza: jsDecode Off-by-One in Octal Escape Handling Enables WAF Bypass

Aliases: CVE-2026-104774

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/corazawaf/coraza/v3 — fixed in 3.8.0

### Summary The `t:jsDecode` transformation in Coraza WAF contains an off-by-one error when parsing octal escape sequences. A backslash character was incorrectly included in the octal number buffer, causing `strconv.ParseInt` to fail for every octal escape sequence and return a null byte instead of the decoded value that would normally be returned. This will cause all JS-escaped payloads to be corrupted, thus leading to the bypassing of these WAF rules when WAF rules that rely on `jsDecode` for normalization are enabled. Therefore, a real-world attack scenario: an attacker could use JavaScript octal escape sequences (`\ooo`) to encode attack syntax. Although the WAF cannot decode these sequences correctly, the target backend (such as a browser or application) can parse them as expected. …

Coraza: Resource exhaustion via deferred file handle accumulation in multipart body processor

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • github.com/corazawaf/coraza/v3 — fixed in 3.8.0

## Summary `defer temp.Close()` sits inside a `for` loop in the multipart processor. All of them stack up and fire together when `ProcessRequest` returns. 500 parts, 500 fds held …

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-3c6w-j9xm-8h2h: Coraza: Unbounded recursion in JSON response body processor causes CPU exhaustion

Coraza: Unbounded recursion in JSON response body processor causes CPU exhaustion

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/corazawaf/coraza/v3 — fixed in 3.8.0

### Summary The JSON response body processor parses response bodies with no recursion limit. `ProcessResponse` calls `readJSON(ss, ignoreJSONRecursionLimit)`, and that constant is `-1`. The guard in `readItems` only fires on `== 0`, so counting down from `-1` (-2, -3, ...) never reaches it. The guard is effectively dead on the response path. The request path is fine: `ProcessRequest` passes the configured limit (default 1024). There is no equivalent directive or default for responses. Parsing a deeply nested JSON response is CPU-bound and its cost grows quadratically with nesting depth. A 512 KiB response (the default `ResponseBodyLimit`) holds about 87,000 nesting levels and takes ~12 s to process, keeping one core busy the whole time. ### Root cause `internal/bodyprocessors/json.go` …

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-wp2g-vpjj-g53r: Excelize ANCHORARRAY: mutually-referencing array formulas recurse unboundedly via re-entrant CalcCellValue, causing a fatal stack overflow
entry.content:
Excelize ANCHORARRAY: mutually-referencing array formulas recurse unboundedly via re-entrant CalcCellValue, causing a fatal stack overflow

Aliases: CVE-2026-107216

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/xuri/excelize/v2 — fixed in 2.11.1-0.20260911060113-ea12859e43c6

### Summary `ANCHORARRAY` (calc.go:15137 on current master) evaluates each cell of the referenced spill range by calling the **exported** `CalcCellValue`, which unconditionally constructs a fresh `calcContext` — fresh entry marker, fresh iterations map, full `MaxCalcIterations` budget (calc.go:896-900). The circular-reference control only exists **within one context**: the entry-exclusion marker and per-ref iteration budget are fields of that single context, and completion-based caching (`formulaArgCache`/`calcRawCache`) only ever stores results of evaluations that *finish*. During a pure cycle no nested evaluation ever finishes, so nothing is ever cached to break the recursion, and each hop re-arms the entire budget. Server panic via missing authority or Host headers in google.golang.org/grpc

Aliases: CVE-2026-84445, GHSA-2v4p-qf9q-27wj

Affected:

  • google.golang.org/grpc — fixed in 1.82.2, 1.83.2, 1.84.0-dev.0.20260825144003-d5a41119e0e3, 1.85.0-dev.0.20260825072537-93e31b48545e

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-5026: Invoking failure to reject ASCII-only Punycode-encoded labels in golang.org/x/net/idna
entry.content:
Invoking failure to reject ASCII-only Punycode-encoded labels in golang.org/x/net/idna

Aliases: CVE-2026-39821

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.13, 1.26.6, 1.27.0-rc.3
  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.55.0

The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6218: Avoid quadratic complexity in resolvePath in net/url
entry.content:
Avoid quadratic complexity in resolvePath in net/url

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-56860, CVE-2026-56860

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.13, 1.26.6, 1.27.0-rc.3

Previously, resolving relative paths containing parent directory ('..') segments performed string conversions and buffer rewrites on each step, resulting in quadratic time complexity and high memory allocation overhead. Now, path resolution operates on a byte buffer using index-based backtracking for '..' segments, eliminating the quadratic time complexity and significantly reducing memory allocations.
